evidence: ch2:182 '~2,000 registered employees, each roughly as active as the canonical scenario (~10 requests/s average...)' reads per-employee, but ch4:60/64 make 10 rps the 2,000-user aggregate (1 req/user per 200 s); the next paragraph uses 10 rps as aggregate.

evidence: ch2:164 claims 'FP8, or BF16 in place of FP16 ... lowers the bytes transferred/stored'. BF16 and FP16 are both 2 B/param and both 989 TFLOPS dense on H100 (ch2:127: 1,979 only with sparsity). Only FP8/FP4 halve bytes and double peak.
fix_instruction: Scope byte-reduction and higher-peak claims to FP8/FP4; note BF16 vs FP16 changes neither bytes nor H100 dense peak.

evidence: ch2:133 lists 'more GPUs (model parallelism or data parallelism)' as a lever for the single-request prefill budget (1.08 s). In-book definition (ch10:9): inference DP = independent replicas to raise throughput; it cannot shorten one request's prefill critical path.
fix_instruction: Say: model parallelism (tensor/pipeline) for per-request prefill latency; data parallelism raises aggregate throughput, not single-request TTFT.
